articles.title: Brewers' Back-To-Back HRs Dent Dodgers' Hopes: 3 Takeaways From NLCS Game 3
articles.summary: The Brewers are one win away from a trip to the World Series for the first time since 1982 after taking a 3-0 series lead over the Dodgers in the NLCS.
articles.body: DODGER STADIUM (Los Angeles) — Milwaukee is on the verge of abolishing baseball’s Evil Empire. The Brewers are one win away from a trip to the World Series for the first time since 1982 after taking a 3-0 series lead over the Dodgers in the NLCS. The Dodgers, backed into the smallest of corners, now face an uphill battle against a well-rounded and red-hot Brewers team that has found its rhythm and is showing no signs of slowing down. The Brew Crew’s season-long combination of timely hitting, strong pitching, power from unexpected places, and a merciless energy has applied pressure on the defending-champion powerhouse, leaving the Dodgers with more questions than answers. Milwaukee, meanwhile, looks determined to finish the job this year after coming up short against Los Angeles in last year’s NLCS. Here are our takeaways from the Brewers’ 6-2 win over the Dodgers in Game 3: 1. Back-To-Back HRs Did Dodgers In Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers did it again. Two days after an epic 12-pitch battle against Yoshinobu Yamamoto that resulted in a walk, Bauers applied the same irritating and relentless pressure to Dodgers southpaw Blake Snell in the seventh inning of Game 3, with Milwaukee trailing Los Angeles, 2-1. No matter what Snell threw at the plate, Bauers wasn’t biting. He fouled off five different pitches — really, Snell’s entire arsenal — in an 11-pitch battle that finally got the best of the left-hander. Snell’s 11th pitch of the at-bat was another meatball, nearly identical to the 97 mph fastball he threw over the heart of the zone to Jackson Chourio on his first pitch of the night. Bauers was all over it. He launched it to right field for a go-ahead, two-run home run that gave the Brewers a 3-2 lead. The entire Brewers dugout spilled onto the field in celebration of Bauers’ first home run of the postseason, knowing it was the advantage they were hunting for against Snell all night. But they weren’t done yet. Batting sixth in the order right after Bauers, Brewers center fielder Garrett Mitchell joined the home-run party with a solo shot to right field off Snell, padding Milwaukee’s lead to 4-2 in the seventh inning. Snell, who had not allowed a single home run across nine starts in the regular season this year, looked exasperated. Milwaukee knew it had Snell on the ropes. Even though Snell tried to get ahead of Milwaukee’s dogged style of play by watching some of the Brewers’ press conferences leading up to his Game 3 start, the extracurricular homework served no purpose between the lines. The Brewers’ back-to-back homers deflated Dodger Stadium, and perhaps even Los Angeles’ dreams of a three-peat. — Thosar 2. Chourio Set Tone With Ambush Dodgers right-hander Blake Snell threw his first pitch in 10 days over the middle of the plate. It was a 97.6 mph meatball, begging to be crushed. Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio didn’t miss. The ball left Chourio’s bat at 106.1 mph and sailed toward the right-field seats, catching everyone off guard. Before fans even settled into their seats with their beverages and snacks, getting ready for a fun night at the ballpark, Chourio slugged his second home run of this postseason and gave the Brewers an instant 1-0 lead. On the road, in a hostile Dodger Stadium environment, the young Brewers star delivered exactly the kind of statement swing Milwaukee needed to keep the pressure on the Dodgers from the jump. It was a reminder that even elite postseason pitchers — Snell entered Game 3 with a 3.23 ERA in 19 career playoff games (16 starts) — cannot afford to make mistakes in the strike zone. Plus, this wasn’t Chourio’s first time. In Game 2 of last year’s NLCS against the Dodgers, Chourio jumped on the first pitch from right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and sent it to deep right field for yet another ambush of a home run. Chourio now owns the most postseason RBI (18) before turning 23 years old. He achieved that mark in just 19 playoff games. Andruw Jones previously held that record with 17 RBI in 45 playoff games. The first-pitch homer completely changed the complexion of the game. The blast Snell gave up to Chourio was the first home run he allowed all season. Snell entered his Game 3 start with the reputation of overpowering hitters. Once he gets going, he’s typically in complete control. We saw that unfold after Chourio’s solo shot. When he got into a groove in the middle innings, Snell retired 14 batters in a row at one point. But once again, the Brewers were just better. — Thosar 3. Will Smith, Nearly The Hero Before Game 3, Brewers manager Pat Murphy mentioned that he thought Dodgers catcher Will Smith had been swinging better than the statistics had shown. The numbers were not pretty. And Smith’s spot in the batting order reflected that. The scuffling Dodgers catcher began the postseason 1-for-23 with a single, a walk and eight strikeouts through his first six games. He was dropped from third in the lineup in Game 1 of the NLCS to fifth in Game 2 and then down to seventh in Game 3, right behind Shohei Ohtani, whose recent struggles also saw the designated hitter sliding down the order. "I know the numbers aren’t there," Murphy said. "But if you do what I do, you watch the swing and you watch his approach, I think he’s looked good." Before the Brewers’ seventh-inning onslaught, in what could have been the swing everyone remembered from Game 3, Smith backed up what his opposing manager saw. The Milwaukee bullpen was virtually unhittable all postseason, entering Wednesday night with a 0.31 ERA this October. But after five scoreless innings from starter Robert Gasser, Murphy’s first reliever of the night didn’t have it in Game 3. Abner Uribe walked Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker to start the sixth inning. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts then pinch-hit Max Muncy for Andy Pages, a surprising decision that reflected the urgency of the moment. The Dodgers entered the night just 2-for-26 with runners in scoring position this postseason. Each of those two hits belonged to Pages. But Uribe appeared to be on the ropes and needed to face the three-batter minimum, so Roberts turned to the platoon advantage with a chance to strike. Instead, Muncy struck out. But Ohtani followed with another walk to load the bases, and Smith finally came through with the hit that had eluded the Dodgers all series, electrifying the 50,708 fans in attendance with a go-ahead, two-run double. The glee, of course, was short-lived. Roberts sent pinch-hitter Josue De Paula to the plate for Miguel Rojas. Murphy countered with lefty DL Hall. Roberts then brought up another pinch-hitter, KIké Hernández, who struck out. Another strikeout followed from Tommy Edman, as the Dodgers’ struggles with runners in scoring position persisted. They failed to build their lead and had emptied their bench, save for backup catcher Hunter Feduccia, to try to go all in with their chance. One inning later, their lead was gone against a relentless Brewers lineup that has countered every punch all postseason. — Kavner

articles.title: ‘They Melt Your Soul Away’: A-Rod Stunned As Brewers Take 3-0 Lead Over Dodgers
articles.summary: A-Rod says the Brewers “melt your soul away" as Milwaukee moves one win from sweeping the two-time defending champion Dodgers in the NLCS.
articles.body: A year ago, the Los Angeles Dodgers swept the Milwaukee Brewers out of the National League Championship Series. Now the Brewers are one win away from returning the favor. Milwaukee beat the Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium to take a 3-0 series lead. The MLB on FOX postgame crew could hardly believe what it was watching. "It’s hard to watch," Alex Rodriguez said. "It reminds me of the first time I saw Mike Tyson get knocked out. You can’t believe what you’re seeing. We were in awe in the green room watching, our mouths open." Rodriguez turned to David Ortiz: "Papi, the Brewers, they simply melt your soul away, and they did that again tonight." The latest blow came from Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser, who who held the Dodgers scoreless for five innings. He allowed three hits and a walk and struck out three before DL Hall threw 2 1/3 scoreless innings for the win, and Trevor Megill got the final four outs for his fourth save of the postseason. "Robert Gasser looked like he didn’t drop a sweat while he was out there facing these Dodgers," Ortiz said. "He was locating his pitches in an incredible type of way, and he just kept coming at them, kept keeping that offense down. He did an incredible job." For Ortiz, Game 3 encapsulated what Milwaukee has done all season. "This is the result of what they did all year long," Ortiz said. "They know how to shut down an offense." Ortiz also singled out Jake Bauers, who has made a habit of wearing down the Dodgers’ best arms. In Game 2, Bauers worked a 12-pitch, bases-loaded walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Then in the seventh inning on Wednesday, with Milwaukee trailing 2-1, he fouled off pitch after pitch from Blake Snell before hitting the 11th one for a go-ahead, two-run homer. "You don’t get to watch many games of the Brewers on TV, but once you are following their steps during this playoff, you get to know how good they are," Ortiz said. "They are deep in every category of the game: pitching, defense, speed. They battle in the at-bat. "Those two at-bats against Yamamoto, and tonight against Snell, those are the most impressive two at-bats that I have seen probably in my whole life." Derek Jeter agreed, saying the most impressive part is who the Brewers are doing it against. "They’ve been doing it all year," Jeter said. "I think the impressive thing is, as was mentioned, they’re doing it against the Dodgers, who swept them last year. It tells a lot about the mentality they have, the resilience they have to come back and face the two-time defending world champion, disregard what happened just 12 months ago, and now you’re up 3-0." Still, Jeter cautioned that the series isn’t over. Nobody knows that better than this crew. In the 2004 American League Championship Series, Ortiz’s Boston Red Sox became the only team in MLB history to come back from a 3-0 series deficit. They did it against Jeter and Rodriguez’s New York Yankees. The Dodgers will try to start their own comeback in Game 4 on Thursday at Dodger Stadium. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Can Dodgers Flip A 3-Game Deficit? Big Papi, Jeter, A-Rod Know It Can Happen
articles.summary: Improbable? Yes. Impossible? No. Just ask the stars who were part of one of MLB's greatest comebacks.
articles.body: If the Dodgers want to make it three straight World Series titles, they must now win four straight games against the Brewers in the NL Championship Series. Improbable? Yes. Impossible? No. Just ask someone who was an integral figure in one of MLB's most historic comebacks. MLB on FOX analyst David "Big Papi" Ortiz, who helped the Boston Red Sox overcome a three-game ALCS deficit in 2004 against the New York Yankees, said it's time for the Dodgers to play like there is nothing to lose. "It's funny how that works, because you feel more pressure at the beginning of the series than when you are 0-and-3 because once you get there, when you hit bottom like that, it feels like you have got nothing to lose," Ortiz said after the Brewers' 6-2 win over the Dodgers on Wednesday night in Game 3. History is certainly not on the Dodgers' side. In all best-of-seven postseason series, teams with a 3-0 lead have gone on to win the series 41 of 42 times, with 32 of those series being sweeps. Only two teams have forced a Game 7 after trailing 3-0 – and only that 2004 Red Sox squad have come all the way back to win. So what would Ortiz tell the Dodgers about taking that first step? "There's no more room to go back. All you gotta do is just move forward. You hit bottom already. Let's just let things happen. Let's not try to get three hits in one at-bat. Let's not try to get three outs in one pitch. Let's go to the flow." On the losing side of that 2004 clash were fellow MLB on FOX analysts Derek Jeter and Alex Rodriguez, who added their perspectives on how the Dodgers should approach Game 4. "The pressure is almost off them right now. Now, they just go out and win a game," Rodriguez said. "And how many times have the Dodgers, over the last five years, won four in a row?… But you got to start with one pitch. You got [Tyler Glasnow] now on the mound tomorrow. If you win tomorrow, you got [Tarik Skubal] in Game 5 and then you never know. "But it starts with the first pitch of the game, and you're playing for your life, and you do not want the Brewers to celebrate on your field." Added Jeter: "Coming into this series, no one thought Milwaukee was going to win three games in a row. But no one expected [the Yankees] to win the first three games in a row against the [Red Sox]. We thought it was going to be evenly matched. If going into that series they said 'we're going to go to seven games', everyone would have believed it. "It's the same thing here. If you're the Los Angeles Dodgers, you cannot take the field thinking that you're down three games. All you have to do is win one game." The Dodgers actually have someone in their dugout who also played in that 2004 series. Manager Dave Roberts was Ortiz's teammate on that 2004 Red Sox team and alluded to that comeback when asked about the Dodgers' chances, starting with Game 4 on Thursday. "It's certainly possible [to overcome a 0-3 deficit]. I've lived it. I think the thing is that our guys have been battle tested, as was that team I was a part of," Roberts said after the Game 3 loss. "They know what's at stake and, you know, we've won four in a row, a number of times this year …. But again, we got to win tomorrow. So that's, that's our only focus."

articles.title: Serena Williams wanted to go vegan; then what changed? When the tennis icon admitted, “I couldn’t quite give up the chicken”
articles.summary: Serena Williams tried changing her diet, but giving up some of her favourite foods proved difficult.
articles.body: Serena Williams tried changing her diet, but giving up some of her favourite foods proved difficult. The tennis legend explored vegan eating after her sister Venus Williams introduced her to raw vegetables and plant-based meals. Serena enjoyed the experience and felt it benefited her body and tennis. However, she could not stick to the diet completely.In a March 2016 interview, she explained why chicken and tacos eventually returned to her meals. She also recalled going vegan during the 2013 French Open, which she won. How Venus Williams introduced Serena Williams to vegan eatingSerena's interest in vegan food grew through her sister Venus, who explored the diet after experiencing health problems. Venus's experience introduced Serena to meals built around raw vegetables and other plant-based foods.In an ESPN interview Serena explained how her sister helped her discover this approach to eating.She said, “She introduced me to a really vegan and raw, kind of really vegetable, whole raw world.”Serena enjoyed trying different foods and noticed changes that she liked. She said the diet had benefits for her game and her body.However, Serena did not suggest that she had completely changed her eating habits overnight. She was exploring a different way of eating and learning what worked for her. Her experience also showed that she could appreciate the benefits of a diet without finding it easy to follow every day.Venus remained an important part of that learning process. Serena explained that her sister continued to educate her about food choices that could help her stay healthy.The two sisters had spent years competing at the highest level of professional tennis. Their careers demanded regular training and physical preparation. Serena's comments showed that she was also paying attention to her diet and looking for ways to take care of her body.She did not credit vegan food with all her success on the court. Instead, she spoke about the positive experience she had while following the diet and her interest in learning more about it.Why Serena Williams could not give up chicken and tacosAlthough Serena liked the vegan diet, sticking to it was another challenge. She admitted that she found it difficult to stop eating some of her favourite foods. “I couldn't quite give up the chicken. And then the tacos kind of creeped back into my life,” Serena told ESPN.Her answer explained why she had struggled to maintain a completely vegan diet. She enjoyed plant-based meals, but she was not ready to give up chicken. Tacos also found their way back into her regular eating habits.Serena was open about the difficulty instead of claiming that she had followed the diet perfectly. She had tried it, enjoyed parts of the experience and still found herself returning to foods she liked.She also clarified that she had made other changes to her diet. Serena said she did not eat red meat and was learning about healthy eating through Venus.“I don't eat red meat and a lot of other stuff, and so I was educating myself through Venus on a lot of things to remain healthy,” she explained.Her comments showed that she continued to think about her food choices even though she struggled to follow a vegan diet. She was interested in eating well, but she had not given up every food that did not fit into a fully plant-based diet.Serena's experience was not a story about rejecting vegan food. She had enjoyed it and recognised benefits during the time she followed it. The difficulty came when she tried to maintain the diet while still wanting foods such as chicken and tacos.She also did not say that she had stopped caring about her diet after returning to those foods. Her comments made it clear that she was still learning from Venus and considering different ways to stay healthy. Serena Williams went vegan during the 2013 French OpenSerena had already tried a vegan diet during a major tennis tournament. She went vegan during the 2013 French Open, where she eventually won the women's singles title.When she discussed that experience with ESPN in 2016, Serena remembered feeling good while following the diet. She also said she had not felt tired during the tournament.“I wasn't tired. It was good. It was really good,” Serena said.Her recollection was positive. She had competed at the French Open while following a vegan diet and remembered the experience as a good one. It gave her a reason to consider trying the diet again.However, Serena did not say that vegan eating was responsible for her victory in Paris. She spoke about how she felt during the tournament rather than claiming the diet had helped her win the title.She also did not present the experience as proof that she could easily follow the diet permanently. Her later admission about chicken and tacos showed that she had struggled to maintain the same approach after the tournament.Still, Serena had not forgotten how she felt in 2013. Three years later, she was considering returning to the diet.“I don't know why I don't do that more often. Maybe this year I need to get back on that,” she told ESPN.Her words suggested that she was open to giving vegan eating another try in 2016. She remembered the experience positively and seemed interested in making it part of her routine again.Serena did not confirm in that interview that she had returned to a vegan diet. She spoke about the possibility of doing so, leaving her plans open.Serena Williams remained open to trying the diet againSerena's 2016 interview offered a straightforward account of her experience with vegan eating. Venus introduced her to raw vegetables and plant-based meals, and Serena found benefits that she liked. But she also admitted that she could not completely give up chicken and eventually returned to eating tacos.Her experience at the 2013 French Open gave her another reason to consider the diet. She remembered feeling good during the tournament and said she had not felt tired. Even after struggling to follow the diet consistently, she remained interested in trying it again.Serena's comments did not suggest that she had settled on one permanent way of eating. She was exploring her options, learning from Venus and making choices based on her own experience.The tennis star also made it clear that avoiding red meat was already part of her eating habits. She continued to educate herself about food and health, even though she could not maintain a fully vegan diet.Her admission about chicken and tacos explained the challenge she faced. articles.title: College Football Week 7 Expert Picks, Predictions For Ohio State-Indiana And More
articles.summary: Here are FOX Sports' expert picks for Week 7 of the college football season.
articles.body: Can No. 4 Ohio State avenge its Big Ten championship game loss to No. 5 Indiana on "Big Noon Kickoff"? Will No. 6 Alabama bounce back against No. 14 Tennessee after a loss to No. 1 Georgia? Elsewhere, a College Football Playoff spot could be on the line when No. 2 Notre Dame visits No. 8 BYU. Austin Simmons leads No. 13 Missouri against his former team, No. 9 Ole Miss. With six matchups between Associated Press Top 25 opponents, Week 7 of the college football season might feature the most exciting slate of the season. We’re breaking down our straight-up picks and the matchups to watch closely throughout the weekend. No. 5 Indiana vs. No. 4 Ohio State When: Saturday, noon ET (FOX)Where: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IndianaLine: Ohio State -3.5 RJ Young: Ohio StateThe best player in the sport is Jeremiah Smith, and Ohio State coach Ryan Day should not be shy about reminding Indiana about that. Laken Litman: Ohio StateThis is my answer for nearly every Ohio State game: The Buckeyes have Jeremiah Smith and Indiana doesn't. Ben Portnoy: IndianaOK, fine, this is probably a bit of a homer pick. I took the Hoosiers to win the Big Ten at the start of the season and I can't stray from that, right? Right. Give me Curt Cignetti's squad in the biggest home game in the history of Indiana football. No. 22 LSU vs. No. 16 Mississippi State When: Saturday, noon ET (ESPN)Where: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LouisianaLine: LSU -14.5 Young: LSUMississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor won't be 100% healthy even if he plays on Saturday. Advantage, LSU. Litman: LSUThe Tigers will rebound at home after an upset loss to Kentucky in overtime last week. Plus, Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor's status is still uncertain. Portnoy: LSUKamario Taylor is still on the mend and while the spread feels pretty big for a matchup of two top-25 teams, I have a hard time seeing the Bulldogs pull this one out. I'll take LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt to get right against what's been just a mediocre Mississippi State defense. No. 14 Tennessee vs. No. 6 Alabama When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC)Where: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TennesseeLine: Alabama -7.5 Young: AlabamaThe Crimson Tide have the better quarterback and wide receiver room. Tennessee must run the ball well to win. Litman: AlabamaEven after last week's loss to Georgia, Alabama looks like a team that could win it all. The Crimson Tide are not going to lose two in a row, especially not against a Tennessee team led by backup quarterback George MacIntyre. Portnoy: AlabamaNothing complicated about this one. Tennessee has real problems at quarterback and absolutely nothing the Vols put on tape last week against Arkansas makes me think they're up for this challenge. Bama rolls big. No. 10 Texas Tech vs. Arizona State When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (FOX)Where: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TexasLine: Texas Tech -14.5 Young: Texas TechTexas Tech has flirted with disaster enough to make me feel nervous, but I think the Red Raiders have an answer for ASU running back Cardae Mack. Litman: Texas TechIn a heated Big 12 race, Texas Tech stays unbeaten with a decisive win over an inconsistent ASU team. Portnoy: Texas TechArizona State and quarterback Cutter Boley have had their moments and I still think Texas Tech is hardly a shoo-in for the Big 12 title, but the Red Raiders are just the more talented team in this one. No. 9 Ole Miss vs. No. 13 Missouri When: Saturday, 3:30 p.m. ET (SEC Network)Where: Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford, MississippiLine: Ole Miss -5.5 Young: MissouriRunning back Jamal Roberts has rushed for at least 200 yards in back-to-back games and quarterback Austin Simmons is good enough to exploit Ole Miss' leaky secondary. Litman: MissouriThe Tigers surprise Ole Miss on the road and further cement themselves as a legit SEC contender. Portnoy: Ole MissI know Ole Miss got run by Florida a few weeks back, but I still think quarterback Trinidad Chambliss is one of the five best players in the sport this year. Austin Simmons has been awesome for Missouri and I think he'll find success against a bad Rebels defense, but Chambliss will make one more play down the stretch to win a shootout. No. 8 BYU vs. No. 2 Notre Dame When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC)Where: LaVell Edwards Stadium, Provo, UtahLine: Notre Dame -10.5 Young: Notre DameBYU will play its biggest game of the season without star tailback and 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martin. I'll take Notre Dame. Litman: Notre DameIn both of these teams' first true test, Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr outduels the Cougars' Bear Bachmeier and removes any doubt that Notre Dame is a real threat to compete for the CFP title. Portnoy: Notre DameSimply put, I don't think BYU has enough firepower without running back LJ Martin to get over the hump here. Notre Dame has been a touch shaky in spurts this fall, but I expect the Irish to handle the Cougars relatively comfortably in this one. Oklahoma vs. No. 15 Kentucky When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (SEC Network)Where: Memorial Stadium, Norman, OklahomaLine: Oklahoma -6.5 Young: KentuckyThe Sooners can't consistently move the ball offensively, and Kentucky has shown it can win close games late. Litman: KentuckyThis is a letdown game for OU after a massive win over Texas last week, while coach Will Stein and Kentucky earn a third SEC road win. Portnoy: KentuckyOklahoma might have won the "Red River Rivalry", but that had far more to do with the horrific play of Texas quarterback Arch Manning down the stretch than anything the Sooners did. Kentucky has won its last two by the skin of its teeth, but the Wildcat offense is simply a far more effective operation right now. No. 20 Houston vs. No. 18 Oklahoma State When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (FOX)Where: TDECU Stadium, Houston, TexasLine: Houston -4.5 Young: Oklahoma StateThe Cowboys are just too explosive, and the Cougars can't win a shootout. Litman: Oklahoma StateIn a game with huge Big 12 standing implications, Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker gets the better of Houston's Conner Weigman and the Cowboys win their fifth consecutive game. Portnoy: Oklahoma StateDrew Mestemaker has come on strong following whatever it is Oklahoma State did when it lost to Tulsa earlier this year. Houston should keep this close down to the wire, but I'll take the Cowboys offense to be the difference. No. 12 UCLA vs. Wisconsin When: Saturday, 7:30 p.m. ET (NBC)Where: Rose Bowl, Pasadena, CaliforniaLine: UCLA -2.5 Young: WisconsinThe Badgers have won four game in a row and will play a UCLA team that needed seven turnovers to win by two points against an Oregon team that started its backup quarterback last weekend. Litman: UCLABruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava is reportedly expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, but backup Ty Dieffenbach does enough to keep the offense rolling. UCLA remains undefeated. Portnoy: UCLAI know Nico Iamaleava is out for the season, but I'm not altogether sure how much that will matter for a UCLA offense that has lived and died by running back Wayne Knight. Wisconsin is riding a high and I like the pieces Luke Fickell has compiled, but I'm giving coach Bob Chesney's bunch the benefit of the doubt. Oregon vs. Nebraska When: Saturday, 11:00 p.m. ET (FOX)Where: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OregonLine: Oregon -7 Young: NebraskaWith quarterback Dante Moore ruled out, Nebraska has the edge. Litman: NebraskaNebraska had Indiana on the rails last week before the defending champs pulled away in the fourth quarter. The Huskers will rebound from the loss against a reeling Oregon team that's trying to keep its season alive. Portnoy: NebraskaDylan Raiola was a disaster last week against UCLA and considering what Nebraska showed against Indiana, I like the Huskers defense to be disruptive in this one. Matt Rhule finally gets a marquee win. articles.title: 'How long will Mirabai Chanu alone keep winning medals for us?' Sports Ministry reviews Asian Games performance; questions injuries, lacklustre show
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's sub-par medal haul in disciplines like athletics and badminton came under scrutiny during the Sports Ministry's review of the country's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's sub-par medal haul in disciplines like athletics and badminton came under scrutiny during the Sports Ministry's review of the country's Asian Games performance on Thursday. In a meeting with the National Sports Federations (NSFs), Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya questioned athlete injuries upon reaching Aichi-Nagoya and the lacklustre effort of some high-profile athletes.India finished fourth in the medal tally at the 2026 Asian Games, pulling ahead after a gold-laden show in the last two days. India bagged 85 medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, including 21 golds, significantly lower than the 106 medals it won at the previous edition in Hangzhou, China.The meeting was attended by Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse, Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President P T Usha, Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao and NSF representatives.The Minister also called for greater responsibility from the NSFs on the sporting performance. He reiterated the need to work with further synergy to sustain India’s sporting excellence.Mandaviya stressed that India needs a continuous pipeline of athletes rather than relying on a handful of medal winners.“How long will Mirabai Chanu alone keep winning medals for us? We need to produce 10 more Mirabai Chanus. Every federation must take this responsibility seriously. We have to identify talent, provide the right training and create an environment in which athletes can progress to the highest level,” the Sports Minister said.As TimesofIndia.com had reported last week, injuries to athletes like hurdler Jyothi Yarraji and triple jumper Praveen Chithravel were brought to attention during the meet. The topic was raised by PT Usha when Athletics Federation of India (AFI) advisor Adille Sumariwalla presented his performance analysis.However, the topic wasn't elaborated on further, with the objective being an overall look at the performance rather than isolated cases.Runner Avinash Sable's fitness came under scrutiny after he failed to start the 5000m, having finished fourth in his pet event, the 3000m steeplechase. He was the defending champion in the steeplechase and had won 5000m silver in Hangzhou.Overall, athletics' gold count fell from six to one this time, while the discipline's total haul of 24 medals was five fewer than at the previous Games.The Boxing Federation of India (BFI), basking in a landmark performance that included an unprecedented three golds, promised more if given "continued institutional support."The organisation's current power struggle between President Ajay Singh and Secretary Pramod Kumar, who have suspended each other over multiple alleged violations, was not discussed.Besides athletics and shooting, badminton has come under scrutiny after producing just one men's team bronze. A major disappointment was defending men's doubles champions Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty crashing out in the first round — a result partly blamed on hectic scheduling that forced players into more than one match within 24 hours.Focus on LA 2028Beyond Asian Games 2026, the platform was also used to assess preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, the 2030 Commonwealth Games and the 2030 Asian Games in Doha.As a path forward, Mandaviya emphasised the need for more sports psychologists, sports science experts and high-performance mental trainers to mitigate the loss of focus that athletes go through when competing on major international stages. He also urged every NSF to introduce more competitions, strengthen athlete preparation, work with dedicated commitment, as well as carry out honest assessment of gaps in performance and administration.Secretary (Sports) Shri Hari Ranjan Rao mentioned that India must aim to finish among the top three at the 2030 Asian Games in Doha, while the 2030 Commonwealth Games, which India is scheduled to host, should be treated as a major national challenge.“We have to strive to finish third at the Asian Games in Doha. articles.title: Top WWE Moments That Could Be Horror Movies
articles.summary: October ushers in the Halloween season, when horror movie fans embrace all things haunting, macabre and terrifying.
articles.body:
October ushers in the Halloween season, when horror movie fans embrace all things haunting, macabre and terrifying.

It also offers wrestling fans a chance to revisit WWE's long history of incorporating horror into its programming—with varying degrees of success.

In celebration of all things that go bump in the night, make the hairs on your arms stand up and send shivers down your spine, relive these moments from the last four decades of WWE television—each worthy of a horror movie in its own right.

Imagine if the giant snake in Anaconda had feasted on Jennifer Lopez's character, or the titular serpent had gotten the best of Jessica Rothe's character in Beware Boiúna .

That was the situation in 1991, when Jake "The Snake" Roberts produced a live cobra and taunted "Macho Man" Randy Savage as the reptile bit into the Hall of Famer's biceps.

Miss Elizabeth and fans in attendance and watching at home looked on in horror, fearing for the former WWE champion's safety.

Savage would recover and get revenge on Roberts, but the attack remains unsettling to watch today—especially for viewers afraid of snakes.

He didn't carry red balloons or ask young fans in the front row if they could float too, but the original incarnation of Doink the Clown was evil nonetheless.

Taking great delight in tormenting fans and wrestlers alike, the evil jester would chuckle one moment, then stare menacingly into the camera the next, his expression suddenly turning deadly serious.

It wasn't one particular moment that made the original Doink terrifying—it was the entire experience. He laughed and joked like an innocent circus clown but behaved like a vile, deceitful horror villain.

Much of that could be credited to Matt Borne and his understanding of how to bring Doink to life. His performance gave the character a sinister depth and helped establish a legacy that endures today.

As long as you stop watching before his ill-fated babyface turn.

Still, Doink evoked Tim Curry's portrayal of Pennywise in 1990's It . Beneath the seemingly harmless clown exterior lurked a sinister edge—a reminder that appearances could be deceiving.

The introduction of The Fiend to the WWE Universe came in what was already essentially a film of sorts.

In the spring of 2019, Bray Wyatt was badly in need of a reboot—and he delivered, introducing the wrestling world to the Firefly Fun House. Channeling Mr. Rogers, he greeted the audience with enthusiasm, but a dark, sinister edge lurked beneath his cheerful demeanor.

Each week, fans ventured further down the rabbit hole until Wyatt introduced one of WWE's most terrifying characters: The Fiend.

Wyatt's alter ego was the stuff of nightmares. With a mask designed by acclaimed horror movie effects artist Jason Baker in collaboration with Wyatt, The Fiend was as unsettling as it was cool.

When he made his in-ring debut at SummerSlam in 2019, fans became even more engrossed in what they were seeing.

With an extraordinarily frightening presentation—and a great concept behind it—The Fiend should have been an even bigger success than it was. Unfortunately, as with many disappointing horror sequels, muddled creative direction diluted what made it one of the most revolutionary horror-themed characters in pro wrestling history.

Still, that first incarnation of the character was pure cinema. Enough that Universal Studios included Wyatt, The Fiend and The Wyatt Sicks spin-off as part of the 2025 Halloween Horror Nights haunted house exhibit.

Imagine believing your brother died in a house fire that also killed your parents. Then, two decades later, your former friend tells you that your brother is still alive—and is coming back for revenge because he believes you started the fire.

That was the scenario The Undertaker found himself in as In Your House: Badd Blood rolled around in October 1997. With the threat of Kane's impending arrival hanging over him, Undertaker watched as The Big Red Monster stalked toward the squared circle, interrupting his Hell in a Cell match with Shawn Michaels.

Kane came face-to-face with The Phenom, and fans saw a rare sight: The Undertaker showing fear.

The Deadman looked genuinely scared as his brother stood across from him, Kane's supposedly burned face hidden behind a red-and-black mask.

Kane dropped 'Taker with a Tombstone piledriver that night, costing him his match against Michaels and setting the stage for one of the most epic story arcs in WWE history.

This storyline was worthy of the big-screen treatment, delivering pure cinema as it built toward the brothers' iconic WrestleMania 14 showdown the following March.

Few fates are more horrific than being buried alive and slowly running out of air. Horror fans have seen that scenario play out countless times, but Ryan Reynolds' performance in 2010's Buried offers a particularly effective portrayal of the desperation it inspires.

In 1991, fans watched in horror as The Ultimate Warrior experienced a similar scenario.

The former WWE champion found himself on the receiving end of a sneak attack from The Undertaker, who emerged from a coffin and jumped him from behind.

From there, Undertaker slammed Warrior into a casket and locked it shut. For several minutes, officials struggled to free Warrior, using tools to pry it open. They eventually freed him, but the scene suggested the damage had already been done.

Undertaker and Warrior never got a major pay-per-view blowoff, leaving the angle without a definitive payoff. Even so, it terrified a generation of young fans and offered a glimpse of how dark The Deadman's character could become.

Big Boss Man would find that out eight years later, but the less said about that one, the better.

articles.title: West Indies’ Hope jokes India series record role a problem as finale looms
articles.summary: Shai Hope worried about excess baggage after latest Player of the Match award in thrilling India-West Indies series.
articles.body:
West Indies captain Shai Hope is worried he may ⁠have to fork ⁠out excess baggage fees after picking up his third Player of the Match award on their tour of India.

The opener’s ⁠unbeaten 102 in the fourth Twenty20 International (T20I) on Wednesday set up a series-levelling win in Hyderabad. He also smashed a century in the ⁠second T20I in Ranchi.

Hope has been in sizzling form throughout the tour, hitting two hundreds in the earlier One-Day International leg. And while he was pleased with his performances, he said he was struggling to fit his ‌awards in his luggage.

“To be honest, they are a bit heavy, and we have got to look at the luggage weight,” he quipped after West Indies prevailed by 24 runs.

“I think we are going to have some problems going back home.”

Hope said getting off to a good start in Hyderabad was key.

“We got 50-plus opening ⁠partnership,” he added. “So it was good for us to ⁠start innings and then obviously we got that foundation, you can express yourself a bit more in the middle period and then try to give the team the best ⁠finish as good as possible.”

Hope clobbered nine sixes in his 50-ball knock and drew the admiration of ⁠his opponents.

“We need to respect what he ⁠has been doing,” India opener Sanju Samson said. “He has been playing some really good cricketing shots, not taking that much risk, and respecting the bowlers as well.”

Hope will look to ‌give himself more baggage problems in Saturday’s series decider in Bengaluru.

West Indies will next visit Bangladesh for a two-Test series later this month. ‌The ‌hosts will breathe easier knowing Hope is being rested ahead of ODI World Cup qualifiers in February.

articles.body: Present at the event were the entire men's T20 team, led by Shreyas Iyer, which played the fourth T20I against West Indies on Wednesday evening and is scheduled to play the fifth and final match against them in Bengaluru on Saturday, along with the women's team, which is due to face Zimbabwe in a T20I in Raipur on Friday, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi met India's Asian Games medal-winners at the Major Dhyan Chand Stadium in New Delhi on Thursday.The athletes presented the PM with memorabilia, including signed jerseys and a bow from 17-year-old archery sensation Kumkum Mohod.PM Modi posed for photographs with the contingent, which was accompanied by senior officials from various sports bodies, including International Cricket Council chairman Jay Shah."You have made 140 crore Indians proud. The biggest success is to make the tri-colour fly high. That's why your success is not just yours but it belongs to crores of our countrymen. I congratulate you on behalf of the entire country," the PM said in his address to the medal winners.India won 85 medals at the Games, including 21 gold, fewer than the 106 medals it secured at the previous edition in Hangzhou. However, the country's debutants made a strong contribution, winning 41 medals."I especially want to congratulate our women athletes, they contributed 38 medals to our tally and 11 of those medals were gold," Modi said, while praising the cricket and hockey teams, as well as the archers who won five gold medals."These medals are not merely numbers; they represent a powerful picture of a New India. Today, India is winning medals even in sports in which we had never won a medal before in the history of the Asian Games. In mixed martial arts, soft tennis, and certain sailing events, our athletes have created history by winning medals for the first time. Friends, now we must reach even greater heights in sports," the Prime Minister added."This time, the Asian Games have been memorable for us in many ways. Both our men’s and women’s hockey teams are present here. Both teams won gold medals this time. And especially our women’s hockey team—you have ended a long wait of 44 years by winning gold. In cricket, both our teams won medals for the second consecutive time. Not only that, they also equalled their own records. In kabaddi, too, both our men’s and women’s teams won gold medals. Similarly, we won five gold medals in archery—and where there is a 'panch' (five), there is God’s blessing. articles.title: 5 under the radar free agents Mets should target during 2026-27 MLB offseason
articles.summary: The Mets should be big players at the very top of the free agent market this offseason, with ace left-hander Tarik Skubal a logical -- and incredibly expensi...
articles.body:
The Mets should be big players at the very top of the free agent market this offseason, with ace left-hander Tarik Skubal a logical -- and incredibly expensive -- target .

Beyond Skubal, there are other intriguing, high-upside starting pitchers such as Michael King .

If the Mets want a starter who profiles more as a No. 2 or No. 3, they could reunite with Clay Holmes , who was a strong clubhouse presence during his two seasons in Queens.

The relief market isn't flush with upper echelon arms, but Adrian Morejon stands out as a potential game-changer.

Looking beyond the major league free agents, Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato is expected to be posted and sign with a big league team this winter. Like Skubal, Sato would be a logical target given New York's glaring need at first base.

But not every player the Mets sign will be a big name.

To that end, here are five under-the-radar free agents David Stearns and the front office should target this offseason...

The Mets should be targeting a franchise-altering ace or at the very least someone (like King) who profiles at the top of the rotation. But after leaving their starting staff short each of the last two seasons -- and that shortage helping to derail each campaign -- New York also needs to bring in a second legitimate rotation option who can pitch in the middle or back end of the rotation.

Soroka, coming off a strong season for the Diamondbacks, could fit the bill.

Once an emerging ace, Soroka's career was derailed after his breakout 2019 season with the Braves due to a torn Achilles suffered during the 2020 shortened season. He didn't return to big league action until 2023, and struggled with inconsistency (4.91 ERA) and injuries (forearm, shoulder, biceps) as he spent time with the Braves, White Sox, Nationals, and Cubs between 2023 and 2025.

This season for the Diamondbacks, Soroka bounced back, posting a 3.41 ERA (3.19 FIP) and 1.08 WHIP in 116.0 innings (21 starts, one relief appearance) while walking 2.3 batters per nine and striking out 8.8 per nine.

In 2026, Soroka's fastball and breaking stuff graded out as elite, via Baseball Savant . His two most utilized pitches were the four-seam fastball and slurve, which he threw 32 percent of the time each. The slurve (which recently became a weapon for Soroka) was especially effective, with hitters slugging just .226 against it (.267 xSLG). Soroka's advanced metrics were a bit of a mixed bag, but he was above average to elite when it came to average exit velocity allowed, chase percentage, strikeout percentage, walk percentage, and hard-hit percentage.

Soroka's injury history and lack of recent innings are concerns, but his upside and age (he'll be entering his age-29 season) are pluses. And if he's a backend option in a rotation with a new ace at the top, the risk is mitigated.

The Mets traded their two left-handed relief cogs ( Brooks Raley and A.J. Minter ) at the deadline because they were both pending free agents, which created an opportunity for Nate Lavender .

Lavender, whose elite extension results in the ball jumping on hitters, ran with his chance while putting up a 1.66 ERA (1.85 FIP) and 0.73 WHIP in 21.2 innings while striking out 10.8 per nine. Hard-throwing Cionel Perez , who is arbitration-eligible, is another left-handed relief option if the Mets tender him a contract .

Either way, it would make sense for New York to pursue another left-handed reliever, with Vesia a potentially strong fit.

Vesia has been a weapon for the Dodgers since 2021, with a 2.66 ERA and 1.08 WHIP in 328.0 innings. He misses bats at a prodigious rate (12.0 strikeouts per nine in his six seasons in Los Angeles), but can also be prone to bases on balls (his career walk rate is 4.3 per nine and it was 5.0 per nine in 2026).

Ahead of his age-31 season and coming off another stellar year, Vesia should be in demand.

The Mets had interest in Loaisiga during the 2024-25 offseason before he ultimately returned to the Yankees. So it would make sense for them to have interest again.

After becoming one of the key cogs in the Yankees' bullpen, Loaisiga's seasons in 2023 and 2024 were seriously impacted because of Tommy John surgery. He returned for the Yanks in 2025, but didn't round back into form until this past season.

In 67.0 innings for the Diamondbacks in 2026, Loaisiga had a 2.42 ERA (2.88 FIP) and 1.03 WHIP while allowing just three homers all year and walking a minuscule 1.7 batters per nine.

Loaisiga relies mainly on a sinker that averages a tick under 98 mph and a changeup that averages 91 mph. He doesn't strike out a lot of batters, but is phenomenal when it comes to limiting hard contact and generating ground balls.

In 2026, Loaisiga was in the 93rd percentile or better in average exit velocity allowed, chase percentage, barrel percentage, hard-hit percentage, and ground ball percentage.

Mahle, who would fit near the back end of the rotation, is coming off a season where he compiled a 3.99 ERA and matching 3.99 FIP for the Giants and Braves over 149.0 regular season innings. He was also terrific in the playoffs for Atlanta, with a 1.35 ERA in 13.1 innings over two starts (one each in the Wild Card Series and NLDS).

He's not someone whose stuff will wow you, but his four-seam fastball has graded out well each of the last two seasons despite not being overpowering. Mahle's other main pitch is a splitter that opposing batters slugged just .354 against in 2026.

Mahle's career ERA in 10 big league seasons with the Reds, Rangers, Twins, Giants, and Braves is 4.01.

Tommy John surgery in May of 2023 wiped out the better part of two seasons for Mahle, but he's exceeded 120 innings in four of his six full big league seasons, and 112 innings in five of six.

The Mets should be seeking a first baseman, and France will be one of the most intriguing names on the market.

What will be interesting to watch is whether the price to sign him stays relatively low because of the offensive player he was during the first seven seasons of his career (108 OPS+), or if it spikes after how France performed for the Padres in 2026.

In 133 games for San Diego, France slashed .295/.363/.502 (.865 OPS, 139 OPS+) with 21 homers and 24 doubles. Was it an aberration or a late breakout from a player in his age-31 season?

A look at France's advanced metrics shows serious improvement in his average exit velocity and hard-hit percentage , so what he did this season wasn't a fluke. At the same time, it's fair to expect some regression going forward given the player he was before 2026.

What's not in question is how good France's first base defense has been the last two seasons. He won the NL Gold Glove in 2025 after being in the 96th percentile in OAA, and followed that up by being in the 93rd percentile in OAA in 2026.

articles.title: Blackhawks vs. Jets: Nazar Returns, But Now No Byram, Lineups, & Watch Game 8
articles.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks (2-5-0) long homestand continues as the division-rival Winnipeg Jets (4-1-1) come to town for a battle at […]
articles.body:
The Chicago Blackhawks (2-5-0) long homestand continues as the division-rival Winnipeg Jets (4-1-1) come to town for a battle at the United Center on Thursday. The game is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. CT and will be broadcast on CHSN.

Thursday marks the first of four meetings between the Blackhawks and Jets this season, with all four occurring within eight weeks. The two teams meet again in Chicago on Nov. 14, then Winnipeg hosts the final two games on Nov. 30 and Dec. 10. Expect some bad blood to brew as the series progresses, with four matchups between Central Division foes in such a short timespan.

The Blackhawks are coming off a much-needed 5-3 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Tuesday, sparked by captain Connor Bedard 's season debut after being cleared to return from offseason shoulder surgery.

Bedard tallied a primary assist and looked sharp in his return, while Teuvo Teravainen and Roman Kantserov each scored twice. It was Kantserov's first career multi-goal and multi-point NHL performance. Tyler Bertuzzi added the empty-netter late in the third period to seal the victory. Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 27 shots in net to earn the win.

After Bedard's return on Tuesday, the Blackhawks will get another massive lineup boost against the Jets. Frank Nazar is eligible to return from a two-game suspension for an illegal check to New York Islanders captain Bo Horvat one week ago. For the first time this season, Bedard and Nazar will both be in the lineup together on Thursday.

Unfortunately, the Blackhawks will be without their No. 1 defenseman against the Jets, as Bowen Byram will miss Thursday's game with an upper-body injury. Head coach Jeff Blashill said Byram is day-to-day after the morning skate. Blashill didn't offer more details on Byram's injury, but it's worth mentioning he took a puck to the helmet/visor in Tuesday's win over Pittsburgh.

The Jets are coming off a 5-2 win over the Minnesota Wild on Tuesday and have only one regulation loss in their first six games this season. Despite star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck remaining away from the team while awaiting a trade, Winnipeg has stormed out of the gates with the top points percentage in the Central Division (.750).

Through six games, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti have done much of the heavy lifting offensively for the Jets. Connor enters Thursday's game tied for second in the NHL with seven goals, while Perfetti is tied for ninth with five tallies. The two wingers have accounted for 12 of the Jets' 18 goals so far this season.

Winnipeg has also benefitted from terrific special-teams play, ranking third in the NHL on the penalty kill (92.3%) and fourth on the power play (31.2%). Head coach Scott Arniel has his team playing well in all facets, so the Blackhawks cannot take a Hellebuyck-less bunch lightly on Thursday.

The Jets won three of four meetings last year, outscoring the Blackhawks 13-10. The season's final two matchups required overtime, with Winnipeg winning both.

articles.title: Breaking down ASU vs Texas Tech Big 12 football game
articles.summary: Arizona State football is 1-1 in Big 12 play. If it wants to stay in the hunt, it will have to pull a major upset this week.
articles.body:
Arizona State football coach Kenny Dillingham admits his team has not met his expectations this season.

The Sun Devils have another chance to do that , but will face a challenge as they'll hit the road to play defending Big 12 champion Texas Tech, which is nationally ranked in both polls and in contention for another conference title.

ASU is coming off a 30-12 win over Hawaii, while Texas Tech had a week off. The Red Raiders have not looked as dominant as they did last season when they reached the College Football Playoff Quarterfinals.

Let's take a closer look at the matchup.

Arizona State (3-2, 1-1) at No. 9/10 Texas Tech (5-0, 2-0)

Time/site : 12:30 p.m. MST, Saturday, Oct. 17, Galaxy Stadium.

TV: FOX Connor Onion (play-by-play), Robert Griffin III (analyst), Alexa Landestoy (sideline). Radio : ESPN 620 AM. (Tim Healey, Jeff Van Raaphorst, Kevin Turner, Jeff Munn).

Series history : Series tied 3-3. The home team has won every game.

Last meeting: ASU upset Texas Tech 26-22 at Mountain America Stadium in 2025. Sam Leavitt threw for 319 yards. Raleek Brown ran for a 1-yard touchdown with 34 seconds left, and Arizona State rallied after blowing a 12-point, fourth-quarter lead.

Arizona State football faces Hawaii in final nonconference game

This is a matchup between the last two Big 12 champions — ASU in 2024 and Texas Tech in 2025. They've also played in the last two years, and the team that lost the head-to-head matchup went on to win the conference.

The Red Raiders enter their Homecoming matchup riding an 11-game home winning streak, which ranks as thesixth-longest currently in college football. A win over the Sun Devils would push the Red Raiders to a 6-0 start for a second straight season and also match the second-longest home winning streak in school history at 12 games (2007-09).

ASU's last win over a top-10 team came against Texas Tech at home last season. The Sun Devils are, however, seeking their first top-10 win on the road since defeating No. 7 UCLA in the Rose Bowl on Oct. 3, 2015.

Kenny Dillingham, ASU (fourth year, 25-19) : Dillingham, 36, is known for his offensive expertise, most notably with quarterbacks. He was the Big 12 Coach of the Year in 2024, the season when ASU won the conference championship.

Joey McGuire, Texas Tech (fifth year, 40-18) : McGuire, 55, is a product of UT-Arlington. Texas Tech was his first head coaching gig in college. He served in an assistant capacity at Baylor for five years before moving to Lubbock.

The passion returns: Dillingham has stressed that while his team has played hard, it hasn't had the same passion as it has in years past. He made some changes this week that he hopes will go a long way toward improving that.

It can convert on third downs : Good numbers here mean a team is moving the ball and taking time off the clock. It's a recipe for success, especially on the road. Out of 138 FBS schools, ASU ranks 128th, having converted just 19 of 64 tries (.297). That's the worst in the Big 12 by a long shot.

Special teams play improves : This was the biggest problem last week. The punting game has been the biggest issue. ASU ranks 135th out of 138 in net punting. The Sun Devils had one blocked last week, with another almost blocked. ASU is also 134th in punt return defense.

The defense gets pressure on Cutter Boley: Texas Tech's defensive line is one of its strengths, while ASU has struggled in the offensive trenches. This is one matchup where the home team has a decided advantage. Senior defensive tackle A.J. Holmes is one to keep an eye on. He should keep the ASU quarterback from getting comfortable in the pocket.

It gets the jump early: The ASU offense has been hit-or-miss and seems best suited for games that are hanging in the balance. It hasn't yet shown the ability to rally from a double-digit deficit.

Wins the takeaway battle : The Red Raiders are on the positive side of the ledger with 10 turnovers gained and eight lost. ASU is on the opposite side at five gained and eight lost, which ranks it 109th in that category. ASU has won that battle just twice this season. Not surprisingly, both were wins (Kansas and Hawaii).

Arizona State : DL My'Keil Gardner, TE Khamari Anderson, LB Zyrus Fiaseu, DB Nigel Pringle, SS Lyrik Rawls, WR Harry Hassmann, DB Jalen Williams, OL Marquis Uni are out. OL Luke Baklenko is doubtful. RB Grayson Rigdon, DL Kirk Vakalahi are questionable.

Texas Tech: RB Cameron Dickey, WR Donte Lee, CB S'Vioarean Martin, S Maddox Quiller, OL Elias Gillen are out. QB Thomas Castellanos, WR Jalen Jones, CB Ashton Hampton, LB Adam Hill, OL Cash Cleveland, OL Hunter Zambrano are questionable.

17 — Explosive plays for ASU wide receiver Reed Harris. That is fifth in the nation. Harris has 11 receptions of more than 20 yards through ASU's first five games — good for fourth in the FBS and first in the Big 12. His 17.35 yards per reception are sixth in the country among players with at least 25 catches this season.

49 —Total tackles for ASU linebacker Owen Long. That ranks him eighth among all FBS defenders. He has three straight games with double-digit tackles.

109 — Career starts Texas Tech's offensive line unit has tallied. Center Sheridan Wilson leads the group with 32 starts over his career, followed by Howard Sampson with 31.

314 — Total number of career tackles for Texas Tech linebacker Ben Roberts. That leads all active FBS players.

1,615 — Career snaps played by ASU defensive tackle C.J. Fite. That is the fifth-most among active interior linemen inthe FBS over the last three-plus seasons.

Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire on ASU quarterback Cutter Boley: "He's a big quarterback, big arm. They're a big play-action team, and he does a good job of hard fakes. We always talk about the safeties not putting their nose where it doesn't belong. A lot of times, those hard fakes pull those safeties down. He's got more than two receivers, but two big-time receivers. He does a really good job of getting them the ball, and I think that 10-to-19-yard range, he's one of the best quarterbacks in the country, and I'm sure what they're talking about is what we're talking about. You've got to be better with the deep ball and create more explosive plays."

Boley on Dillingham's challenge about being more passionate: "Everybody on the leadership council and everybody who considers themselves a leader on this team really took that as a challenge. You could tell the passion we had today, just having fun. Still being locked and dialed in, but also being able to have fun and play free."

Dillingham on playing in Lubbock : "An unbelievable environment. They got a great tradition there. I know they sold out a game on a Friday night, which is impressive. That just tells you that this place is going to be rocking here on Saturday. They're 5-0, They are one of the best teams in the country, a top-10 team in the country. They have everything positive there. So it is a great challenge for our guys, a great challenge for our staff, and it's going to be an unbelievable environment to go play in."

Texas Tech 27, Arizona State 21 : This is by far the toughest team ASU has faced this season, and playing the Red Raiders on their turf makes it an even more formidable challenge. The Sun Devils improved last week, but that was against a lower-tier Mountain West Conference foe. This is a different level of challenge. The Red Raiders will also have plenty of incentive after taking the Sun Devils lightly a year ago and losing to them in Tempe.

articles.summary: The Steelers could face Tampa Bay's rookie quarterback in Week 6 as Baker Mayfield continues to recover from a thumb injury. Here's the latest on the Buccane...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers could have a different quarterback to prepare for when they visit the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.

Baker Mayfield remained sidelined at Thursday's practice as he works his way back from a dislocated thumb suffered in Tampa Bay's Week 3 loss to Minnesota. The Buccaneers quarterback was initially expected to miss at least three weeks, though a potential early return had emerged as a possibility.

That return now appears less likely. Mayfield's ability to grip and throw the football remains a key factor in determining when he can get back on the field, and his latest absence leaves Tampa Bay preparing for another game without its starting quarterback.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels is expected to start against Pittsburgh unless circumstances change, according to NFL reporter Rick Stroud. Daniels would make his third consecutive start after leading Tampa Bay to its first win of the season against Dallas last Thursday.

Daniels has completed 38 of 55 passes for 337 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions across his previous three games. He has added 87 yards on 16 rushing attempts.

Mayfield has thrown for 615 yards and two touchdowns against two interceptions this season while completing 63.5% of his passes.

articles.title: 10 general manager candidates if the Saints move on from Mickey Loomis
articles.summary: Gayle Benson singled out longtime general manager Mickey Loomis in her public criticism of the Saints' performance. Which candidates could replace him?
articles.body:
Gayle Benson singled out longtime general manager Mickey Loomis in her public criticism of the New Orleans Saints ' performance, but that doesn't mean she would really fire him, right? Loomis is the longest-tenured executive in the league (if you don't count owners at the controls like Jerry Jones) and Benson has gone on the record as calling his hiring one of the best things to ever happen to the franchise. But he's guided the Saints to a 56-81 record when Sean Payton wasn't coaching his team. If the end is in sight for Kellen Moore after just a year and a half on the job, Loomis will be 1-for-3 on hiring head coaches. A new coach should get a fresh start with a new general manager.

Whether Loomis is dismissed, pushed into retirement, or "promoted" to a position without any control of the roster, replacing him should be on the table. But which candidates could replace him? Here are ten names to know.

Alexander spent decades working under legendary Baltimore Ravens general manager Ozzie Newsome, and he's found success as the Los Angeles Chargers assistant GM in recent years. He's an experienced scout and helped build two Super Bowl-winning teams before leaving for a promotion; Alexander ran the New York Jets player personnel department from 2019 to 2023 when they hit big on first-round draft picks like Garrett Wilson and Sauce Gardner. But he " respectfully declined " to interview for the Minnesota Vikings GM opening this offseason in order to see things through with L.A. Their 0-5 start may lead to organizational turnover, and if he's open to a move to lead his own team, the Saints should give him a look.

Ireland feels like the early favorite if the Saints go with an in-house promotion; he's worked as a general manager before, learning some painful lessons with the Miami Dolphins on the way to a 46-50 finish. He has flourished while running the Saints' college scouting department since 2015 and has influence in the front office as the team's assistant general manager. Ireland has interviewed for several GM openings around the league over the years but remains with New Orleans. It's tough to see him staying if the Saints pass over him.

The other popular pick for a promotion? That's Harley, the team's senior vice president of football operations and assistant general manager. He's one of the two lieutenants to Loomis, along with Ireland, and is best known for his work managing the salary cap. Harley also has experience negotiating contracts, managing the roster, and coordinating with both the pro and college scouting departments. He's been a key asset in the front office for a very long time. Harley has been with the team for 18 years and would be a familiar voice to Benson.

Here's a dark horse to watch if the Saints stay focused on in-house candidates. Parenton, the vice president of pro personnel, is chiefly responsible for scouting free agents, trade targets, waiver claims and every other avenue of adding talent. He's also responsible for advance scouting reports of upcoming opponents. Parenton has worked for the Saints since 2012 and does a lot to bridge the gap between the front office and the coaching staff. Don't overlook the Tulane grad from Thibodaux.

Fontenot got his start in the Saints' organization, and at one point looked like the heir-apparent if Loomis ever chose to step down. Instead, the Lake Charles native and Tulane graduate who started working for New Orleans as a scout in 2003 went turncoat with the Atlanta Falcons. He drafted well but couldn't find a coach or steady quarterback, and was dismissed after going 36-48. Maybe a homecoming (and lessons learned from that experience) could be good for him.

Cody Rager. Sean Payton made sure to bring Rager with him to the Denver Broncos as vice president of player personnel; before that, he worked for the Saints since 2015 and climbed the ladder to become Ireland's right-hand man. He's an experienced talent evaluator who the organization knows well.

Louis Riddick. The longtime ESPN commentator hasn't worked in an NFL front office since 2013, but he does have ambitions of running his own team someday. Riddick has interviewed for multiple general manager openings in recent years and could have some appeal with an outside perspective.

John McKay. We're continuing the theme of outside candidates. The Los Angeles Rams assistant general manager has done good work just across town from Alexander and the Chargers, having worked under Les Snead for 10 years. He's led the Rams' pro scouting department and has received interview requests from teams like the Vikings.

RJ Gillen. A 12-year member of the San Francisco 49ers front office, Gillen was recently promoted to assistant GM and appears to be a rising star in the organization. He runs the player personnel department and manages day-to-day operations while advising John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan on roster construction. He has a broad range of experiences and could be well-suited to an executive role. Gillen also played college football at LSU from 2007 to 2010.

Drew Brees. Plenty of Saints fans have pointed to what Matt Ryan does with the Atlanta Falcons (he's a full-time employee titled "President of Football" handling communication between ownership, the front office, and the coaching staff) and said Brees should take the same path. You just have to wonder how committed he is to calling games for FOX after spending years trying to break into broadcasting. Brees could have taken an easier path to coach or work in football operations, but he seems to have a real passion for his current role. Even if he was open to it, the Saints would need someone to work as a GM.

articles.title: Washington Commanders open practice window for key reserve linebacker
articles.summary: Linebackers Jordan Magee is back at practice following a hamstring strain that landed him on injured reserve
articles.body:
Jordan Magee is getting back to practice. That's a plus for the Commanders, who formally opened his 21-day window to return off injured reserve.

He was placed on IR following a hamstring strain suffered in a Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. He's an important depth piece and core special teams player who was missed while he was out.

Washington's linebacker depth was tested during that stretch with Frankie Luvu missing time and Leo Chenal suffering a fractured neck that ended his season.

Magee should be the primary backup if he's able to return off IR. If he isn't activated before the end of this 21-day window, he'll be placed on season-ending injured reserve.

The Commanders have return to play guidelines that generally involved a ramp-up period, though it varies in length based upon the nature of the injury and a player's health status.

Getting Magee before a Week 6 clash with San Francisco is probably an unfair expectation, but it's not impossible. A return after the bye, though, seems more likely.

Also, head coach Dan Quinn said that cornerback Trey Amos and running back Jeremy McNichols, who are also on IR and in the midst of their practice windows, are expected to be full participants in practice this week. Same with safety Nick Cross, who is on the active roster. The Commanders brought defensive lineman Deatrich Wise back from IR last week and he was a key player up front.

articles.title: Players to watch, predictions as Notre Dame football visits BYU
articles.summary: Along comes the first game on the 2026 Notre Dame football schedule that we've all been waiting on - a visit to undefeated and eighth-ranked BYU.
articles.body:
SOUTH BEND – Now this is a college football Saturday.

We made it to the one game on the Notre Dame football schedule that everyone has pointed to as the true start for the 2026 Irish season. No more overwhelming another overmatched Big Ten opponent. No more one-sided affairs against academic-minded schools that seem more like scrimmages (sorry, Rice and Stanford). No more telling your college football friends and neighbors that No. 2 Notre Dame (6-0) will show what it is — who it is — come mid-October.

It's No. 8 and undefeated Brigham Young (5-0). It's under the lights in a cool, crazed venue. It's the Irish going to Utah for the first time in decades. It's everything we've waited for since everything started in the Upper Midwest on Labor Day weekend. It's college football at its finest.

Here are four players (OK, a few more) to keep an eye on to make this prime-time matchup worth watching.

From left to right – Will Black (LT), Anthonie Knapp (LG), Ashton Craig (C), Sullivan Absher (RG) and Guerby Lambert (RT) have started the last five games together. We were cautioned in August that it would take time for this new group that featured only one starter back at his original position from 2025 (Craig), before it all looked like it was supposed to look.

It looks good now. Notre Dame ran for 177 yards at Purdue, 241 at North Carolina, then rolled up 361 at home against Stanford. That's good. Better yet is the group has allowed quarterback CJ Carr to be sacked only twice through six games (399 offensive plays). One came on the opening drive of the season against Wisconsin. That's staggering.

This is a test your manhood game against a defense ranked eighth overall and 10 th against the run. It's the kind of contest where Notre Dame must use its size advantage — the line averages 6-foot-6.2, 316.2 pounds against a BYU front three that averages 6-3.3, 295 pounds, to wear down the other guys. String together long scoring drives. Run the ball with that bevy of backs. Flex their collective muscles.

We start the second half of the season the way we started the first half of the season highlighting the same Irish defensive player who can make a difference. It was the 6-5, 253-pound senior from Boston then; it's the 6-5, 253-pound senior from Boston now, but for wildly different reasons.

In early September, we didn't know what the Irish had in Traore, who had the potential to be someone you had to account for on every play. He had the chance to get there, but would he get there?

He's there. Traore has not so quietly become one of the top edge rushers in the country. He's fifth on the team in tackles (17), tied for first with 5.5 tackles for loss, first in sacks (3.5) and forced fumbles (one). He also leads the team with eight quarterback hurries. The next closest Irish has two. How? Simple, Traore said after terrorizing Stanford. He plays like he practices — all out on every play. Can't stop him during the week; can't stop him on Saturdays.

Traore was good the first half of the season. He could be even better the second half. For opposing offenses, that's a frightening thought. Beast mode loading.

What strikes you about Bachmeier, besides the numbers he's posted since transferring from Stanford, is his number. Not many quarterbacks around the country sport No. 47, his first jersey when he started football at age 5. He was a middle linebacker until eighth grade. When he moved to quarterback, he kept the number. Gave him an attitude. A middle linebacker's mindset.

With standout running back LJ Martin out with an injury in this one, even more is expected/demanded of the 6-2, 230-pound sophomore from Murrieta, California. Bachmeier has carried 36 times for 239 yards and four touchdowns. He's thrown for 1,033 yards and eight touchdowns. Stop Bachmeier, and the Irish likely stop the Cougars.

This is the highest-ranked team Bachmeier and BYU has faced since a 34-7 loss to then-fourth ranked Texas Tech in the Big 12 championship game last December. Bachmeier is coming off season highs for completions (22), attempts (30) pass yards (329) and rush yards (109) in last week's win over Iowa State. It's like the Cougars have found something without Martin.

Let Bachmeier get going in both the run and the pass game, and it could be a long night for one of the nation's elite defenses.

Don't sleep on the defense for a program that's often known for what it does on the other side of the football. They can cause havoc and turn you over in the shadows of the Wasatch Mountains as well.

Brigham Young ranks in the top 10 in three major defensive statistical categories — total (eighth), scoring (ninth) and rush (10 th ). The ringleader is Uluave, a 6-1, 230-pound senior from South Jordan, Utah who spent three seasons at Cal, where he was a tackling machine. Uluave earned first team All-Atlantic Coast Conference honors last season after making 100 stops for the Golden Bears. He returned home this season and picked up where he left off.

One of 13 linebackers on the roster, which includes two sets of brothers, Uluave finds the ball, gets the ball and makes the stop. His 26 tackles lead the team. He tied his season high with six tackles in the win over Iowa State, and has tallied six, five, six and six in the last four games. He and the BYU defense will be tested by Notre Dame in ways they haven't been tested. With Uluave lurking from his middle linebacker spot, the Cougars might pass that test.

Notre Dame 27, BYU 13: Banged-up Cougars hang around for a while before Irish pull away late.

Notre Dame 24, BYU 14: The Irish have been waiting for a challenge like this and will deliver in a challenge like this the way a veteran, mature, focused team should deliver.

Notre Dame 31, BYU 17: This game has Virginia Tech 2018-like energy. Marquee game, at night, the hosts should come out fired up. I don't know if we get a 98-yard touchdown run after that (Jonaz Walton encore maybe?), but the better team — Notre Dame — will pull away in the second half to get the first of what they hope will be several season-defining wins.

Follow South Bend Tribune and NDInsider columnist Tom Noie on X (formerly Twitter): @tnoieNDI. Contact Noie at tnoie@sbtinfo.com
