articles.title: Jalen Hurts shares how he built chemistry with Eagles WR Darius Cooper
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts spent an extra hour with Darius Cooper before the Eagles' London game, then connected with the receiver for a 62-yard touchdown
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts spent an hour meeting one-on-one with Darius Cooper last week, and the Eagles quarterback believes the results showed up against Jacksonville. In a video from Dave Uram of SportsRadio WIP and KYW Newsradio , Hurts pointed to Cooper's performance as evidence the time together paid off. The second-year receiver caught two passes for a team-high 71 yards in Philadelphia's 19-17 loss in London, including a 62-yard touchdown from Hurts.

That score came on third-and-10 in the second quarter and gave the Eagles a 14-7 lead. It was Philadelphia's longest offensive play of the game and Hurts' only touchdown pass. Cooper has made his limited receiving opportunities count this season. Through five games, he has seven receptions for 130 yards and four touchdowns, including two scores against the Rams and the game-winning catch against Tennessee.

His involvement increased in London with DeVonta Smith and Marquise Brown inactive. Cooper played 53 of Philadelphia's 62 offensive snaps, the most among Eagles receivers, but drew three targets. His touchdown supplied an explosive play for an offense that finished with 232 total yards.= Hurts' account offers a look at the individual work behind their developing connection. Philadelphia has needed contributions from its depth receivers while injuries reshape the offense, and Cooper has repeatedly delivered in scoring situations.

The next opportunity comes Sunday against Carolina. As the Eagles try to end a three-game losing streak, a more consistent connection between Hurts and Cooper could turn occasional explosive plays into a more dependable passing attack.

articles.title: LaMelo Ball earns Magic Johnson comparison from new Minnesota teammate
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves acquiring LaMelo Ball from the Charlotte Hornets this offseason was one of the bigger moves that occurred. Many NBA fans and progn...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves acquiring LaMelo Ball from the Charlotte Hornets this offseason was one of the bigger moves that occurred. Many NBA fans and prognosticators believe that Anthony Edwards needed a second All-Star-caliber player on the team to truly contend in the Western Conference. The Timberwolves were ultimately able to get Ball, who will serve as one of the team's primary playmakers.

Ball appeared on Anthony Edwards' "Believe That Awards," hosted in partnership with PrizePicks on his YouTube channel. When asked what he plans to incorporate into the Timberwolves team culture following his stint with the Hornets, Ball kept it plain.

"We done been playing," Ball said. "They, they already see what I can do. Yeah. I know what they can do. Just gonna put that together and-"

Jaden McDaniels chimed in and simply said, "Magic Johnson," which caused a positive response from the rest of their teammates in the room.

"Running and gunning, man. Yeah. Running and gunning," Ball said with a smile.

Over his first few seasons in the league, LaMelo Ball has emerged as one of the NBA's best playmakers at the point guard position. Last season, Ball played in 72 games and averaged 20 points, 7.1 assists, and 1.2 steals while shooting 36.8% from the 3-point range. For his career, Ball averages 7.3 assists per game, with his career high being 8.4 assists in the 2022-2023 season.

LaMelo Ball makes his debut with the Minnesota Timberwolves next Wednesday in a nationally televised ESPN matchup when the team faces off against Giannis Antetokounmpo and the new-look Miami Heat.

articles.title: 5 Takeaways From Spurs’ Preseason Win Over Suns
articles.summary: San Antonio Spurs’ 123-103 win over the Phoenix Suns showed how the Spurs are building their offense around Victor Wembanyama and three guards. The result wa...
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs' 123-103 win over the Phoenix Suns showed how the Spurs are building their offense around Victor Wembanyama and three guards. The result was encouraging, though the starting lineup's slow start showed that the new additions still need time to gel.

Phoenix rested several regulars, including Devin Booker , which limits the meaning of the performance. Even so, Wembanyama, Stephon Castle and Carter Bryant gave San Antonio plenty to examine before the regular season.

1. The Three-Guard Lineup Needs More Time

San Antonio started De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper alongside Devin Vassell and Wembanyama. The lineup gave the Spurs three ball handlers, but the opening minutes showed how difficult it could be to involve everyone. The starters made only one of their first 10 shots and scored 3 points before the first substitution.

San Antonio recovered and led 60-49 at halftime, but the slow start showed that talent alone will not make the lineup work. Fox, Castle and Harper must learn when to run the offense, move without the ball and play through Wembanyama.

Fox played only 19 minutes after returning from a hip issue, while Harper is still adjusting to the NBA. Building that chemistry will take time. The Spurs must also rebound and run in transition to get the most from the smaller lineup.

2. Victor Wembanyama Gave the Offense a Reliable Option

Wembanyama scored 19 points on 9-of-14 shooting in 23 minutes while adding four blocks and three assists. His efficiency gave San Antonio a dependable option when its guards struggled to create clean shots.

How the Spurs use Wembanyama will matter as much as his production. Fox, Castle and Harper can beat defenders off the dribble, but those drives become harder when opponents pack the paint. Wembanyama can punish that coverage near the rim or draw help and open space for teammates. The guards must find those openings instead of forcing difficult shots.

His defensive value was just as clear, though San Antonio cannot expect him to erase every mistake. The guards must limit penetration, and the other players must help finish possessions with rebounds. Wembanyama has a greater impact when the defense supports him, rather than relying on his blocks to save broken plays.

3. Stephon Castle Scored Without His Jumper

Castle finished with 18 points and made 14 of 15 free throws despite shooting 2-of-5 from the field and missing both three-point attempts. His ability to draw contact gave San Antonio another scoring option when his jump shot was not falling.

That skill helps a lineup built around several young guards. Castle can pressure defenders and get to the line, but opponents may eventually back off, forcing him to shoot from outside. His progress as a shooter will shape how teams defend him when he does not have the ball.

A more dependable perimeter shot would leave defenses with fewer chances to help off Castle. It would also open driving lanes for Fox and create more room for Wembanyama inside.

4. Rebounding Helped Protect Smaller Lineup

San Antonio outrebounded Phoenix 56-44 and collected 12 offensive rebounds. Rookie center Tarris Reed Jr. led the Spurs with 9 boards, showing that the team could find rebounding help beyond its starting lineup.

That margin matters because a three-guard lineup can struggle against bigger frontcourts. Wembanyama cannot contest every shot and secure every rebound, especially when opponents pull him away from the basket.

Reed's contribution gave San Antonio another option, though Phoenix's missing regulars make the result less convincing. The Spurs still must show they can control the glass against stronger teams.

5. Carter Bryant Made a Case for Rotation Minutes

Bryant scored 16 points in 16 minutes, made four of seven three-pointers and added five rebounds and two blocks. His shooting could create space and help solve one of the Spurs' 3 problems when opponents send more defenders toward the guards and Wembanyama.

One strong performance does not guarantee Bryant a regular role. San Antonio rested several rotation players, giving more minutes to its younger core .

Bryant must defend consistently, make quick decisions and hit open shots against regular-season pressure. If he does, his shooting and defensive activity could give the Spurs another useful lineup option.

San Antonio has promising players, but the three-guard lineup must still work against a full-strength opponent. Wembanyama gives the Spurs a clear offensive option, Castle's ability to draw fouls provides another route to points, and Bryant could improve spacing.

The rebounding advantage also mattered, though Phoenix's absences limit what the result proves. San Antonio's next challenge is turning those individual strengths into a lineup that holds up when the regular season begins.

articles.title: Simon Edvinsson Trade Still Live Despite Horcoff’s Zero Interest
articles.summary: Shawn Horcoff says zero interest in trading Simon Edvinsson, but Pierre LeBrun still sees a trade. #RedWings
articles.body:
Simon Edvinsson is still unsigned, and the Detroit Red Wings keep insisting he is not going anywhere. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff used his Wednesday press conference to shut the door on a trade. "I have zero interest in trading Simon Edvinsson," Horcoff said . "I want to keep him." That should not come as a surprise.

Pierre LeBrun is not buying that it ends there. Joining Jay Onrait on TSN's SportsCentre on Thursday, the TSN hockey insider said of Horcoff's comments, "It is interesting that Shawn Horcoff told the Detroit media what we've been saying all week, that he has no intention of trading Simon Edvinsson, and that he intends to sign him but I still think that the longer it goes, a trade is still possible."

Red Wings must sign Simon Edvinsson by Dec. 1

Edvinsson, 23, played 72 games for Detroit last season and put up nine goals and 16 assists with a plus-12 rating. His 22:21 of ice time a night was the second-highest total on the roster, which is the real reason this standoff matters.

With Alex DeBrincat locked up on a seven-year, $91 million extension , the next order of business for Horcoff is Edvinsson. The defenseman is still a restricted free agent, and Detroit has until Dec. 1 to get him signed. Miss that deadline and Edvinsson cannot play in the NHL at all this season.

Edvinsson has been in Sweden skating with Frolunda HC of the SHL, and TSN's Chris Johnston reported on Oct. 13 that he is heading back to North America to work with a trainer he trusts. Johnston was careful to say the trip is not a signal that a contract is close.

Ten teams have already called about a Simon Edvinsson trade

LeBrun is the insider who mapped that market. On Oct. 8 he reported that at least 10 teams had checked in on Edvinsson, with the Boston Bruins among them, and that Detroit was telling every one of them it still intended to extend him. A "sizeable gap" in salary is what has held the talks up.

That is why LeBrun's Thursday comment carries weight. Horcoff can say he has zero interest, but the man who knows which teams have called thinks time changes the math. If Edvinsson is still unsigned in a few weeks, Boston and nine other clubs are still on the other end of the phone.

The Philadelphia 76ers are currently in the end stages of their preseason as they prepare for the upcoming 2026-27 campaign. The 76ers have plenty of star power on their roster after their offseason revamp, headlined by Jaylen Brown , who was acquired by the team from the Boston Celtics.

Brown has wasted little time ingratiating himself with the local community in Philadelphia, and that trend continued with a recent appearance at multiple high schools alongside teammates Justin Edwards, Adem Bona, and Tacko Fall.

Brown was known for his work in the community during his time with the Celtics, and clearly, he has no plans on stopping that now that he is on a new team.

Meanwhile, on the court, questions persist about how the 76ers' new "big five," headlined by Brown, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and VJ Edgecombe, will fit together on the court, that is, if they are able to share the court much at all (injuries are of paramount concern).

There are also big questions about the relative lack of elite outside shooting on this 76ers' roster, as well as whether their defense will be able to hold up.

Still, there's no doubting the amount of star power on the team's roster, with the front office flipping Paul George and a couple of draft picks for Brown and then signing James to a minimum contract a few weeks later in free agency.

The 76ers figure to be one of the most fascinating basketball experiments in recent history, with a wide variety of outcomes on the table for the upcoming season.

Philadelphia is slated to begin its new season on October 20 vs the New York Knicks on the road.

articles.title: Week 6 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: DK Metcalf vs. Jaylen Waddle
articles.summary: By comparing their target volume, receiving production, touchdown potential, and overall offensive situations, fantasy managers can get a clearer picture of...
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers often find themselves weighing athletic dominance against explosive open-field speed. A prime example of this dilemma is the head-to-head comparison between Jaylen Waddle and DK Metcalf. On paper, both receivers possess league-winning, WR1 upside. Fantasy value is rarely dictated by draft capital or name recognition alone.

Through five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, both pass-catchers have posted nearly identical total fantasy outputs. Choosing between Waddle and Metcalf isn't just a choice between two players. It comes down to either trusting a high-volume route runner who can turn short touches into home runs, or banking on a classic alpha perimeter receiver who leans on high air yards and touchdown conversion.

Can Waddle Turn Speed Into Consistent Fantasy Production?

Operating in Sean Payton's system gives Waddle manufactured touches through designed screens, jet sweeps, and any other creative ways they can get the football in his hands. Denver loves to scheme and gets the ball into space quickly to allow the playmakers to rack up yardage after the catch. Passing volume with the Broncos offense could fluctuate depending on how much Payton decides decide to lean on the ground game.

Can Metcalf's Size & Scoring Ability Give Him the Edge?

Now operating in Pittsburgh's offense under Mike McCarthy, Metcalf is being moved around the formation to create size mismatches on the outside and in the slot. Standing 6'4" and weighing 235 pounds, Metcalf's primary fantasy appeal lies in his downfield leverage and high-value red-zone opportunities. While efficiency issues and early-season drop rates have capped his game-to-game floor, his commanding air-yard share ensures that he is always a candidate for multi-touchdown upside.

The Numbers Reveal a Narrow Gap in Fantasy Production

Separated by 0.1 total PPR points over five games, neither receiver has established a significant statistical advantage over the other. Both are averaging right at 9.0 points per game , which currently places them in the mid-WR3 territory for fantasy formats.

While their baseline fantasy points match, Metcalf's share of team air-yards gives him a slight edge in yardage, while Waddle's reliance on receptions makes him slightly more sensitive to total target volume.

Target Share Parity: Both receivers command a 21% target share within their respective passing offenses.

Air Yards Advantage: Metcalf holds a distinct lead in Air-Yards Share (32% vs. 21%). Because Metcalf is targeted further downfield on vertical routes and perimeter go-routes, his targets yield higher expected fantasy value per catch.

High-Value Touches: Metcalf leads in high-value opportunities with 4 end-zone targets compared to Waddle's 3 red-zone targets, giving Metcalf a structural advantage and increased touchdown probability.

Which Receiver Has the Easier Matchup in Week 6?

One Defensive Weakness Could Decide This Fantasy Showdown

Waddle's Matchup: Seattle presents a tough challenge. Their defense ranks among the top 3 against fantasy receivers in 2026. Their two-high safety coverage limits deep explosive plays, forcing Denver to throw underneath into tight zone windows.

Metcalf's Matchup: Facing Tampa Bay offers an easier route to solid fantasy production. The Bucs run aggressive defensive fronts that leaves secondary cornerbacks in single coverage exposed on the outside. Metcalf's physical size creates direct advantages against Tampa Bay's secondary.

Final Verdict: Who Should Fantasy Managers Start?

Higher Floor: Waddle offers the more dependable weekly workload in full-PPR formats due to Payton's short-area play design in Denver.

Higher Ceiling: Metcalf has the easier matchup in order to produce a 20-point fantasy performance thanks to his dominant air-yard share (32%) and deep chemistry with Aaron Rodgers.

articles.summary: The SMU Mustangs are launching the first Division I men's lacrosse program in Texas in 2028, to compete in the ACC.
articles.body:
SMU announced Thursday, Oct. 15, that it's launching the first Division I men's lacrosse program in Texas.

The program, which will officially begin competition in 2028, will become the ACC's sixth lacrosse program.

"This is a historic moment for SMU and for the sport of lacrosse," SMU athletic director Damon Evans said in the announcement. "We are proud to be the first Division I school to bring men's lacrosse to Texas, a sport that has tremendous growth potential across our state. This is a bold investment that will bring another elite program to our campus, and we expect to compete and win immediately."

The Mustangs will enter the fray in a sport that has largely been dominated historically by the Northeast. It will immediately part of a conference with some of the deepest roots in lacrosse, with the ACC currently being represented by Notre Dame, North Carolina, Duke, Virginia and Syracuse.

ACC commissioner Jim Phillips said in a statement, published by SMU:

"SMU President Jay Hartzell, Director of Athletics Damon Evans and the entire Mustang leadership team should be applauded for their substantial investment in, and continued commitment to, providing increased opportunities for student-athletes. The addition of men's lacrosse is an exciting step forward for SMU's athletics program and campus community. The ACC is widely recognized as the nation's premier men's lacrosse conference, and we look forward to welcoming the Mustangs to our men's lacrosse ranks."

articles.summary: Florida football is among 25 FBS schools to have their offensive line named to the 2026 Joe Moore Award Midseason Honor Roll.
articles.body:
Florida football's offensive line was named to the 2026 Joe Moore Award Midseason Honor Roll, the award's organization announced on Wednesday afternoon.

The Gators have one of 25 offensive line units named to the midseason list and one of six SEC teams, joined by Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Missouri, and Tennessee.

The offensive line unit, led by starters Bryce Lovett, Knijeah Harris, Harrison Moore, TJ Shanahan Jr. and Emeka Ugorji, currently ranks fourth in the SEC in sacks allowed with eight, while PFF credits only four sacks allowed by the line. According to PFF, the unit has also allowed just five quarterback hits and 21 QB hurries on the season, while putting up a run-blocking grade of 70.2 — good for 21st in the country.

Thanks in large part to the O-line, Florida is ranked 12th in scoring offense, 18th in total offense, 23rd in passing efficiency, 25th in passing offense and 34th in rushing offense among FBS schools so far this season.

PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida vs South Carolina in Week 6

Founded in 2015 and presented by the Foundation for Teamwork, the Joe Moore Award is given to the most outstanding offensive line unit in college football — the only major award in the sport given to a group rather than an individual.

There are no personal statistics to chase and no individual names on the trophy, only the standard Joe Moore demanded: toughness, teamwork, and five men playing as one. It's voted on by the people who would know — every FBS offensive line coach, former linemen in the media and a legacy committee of the men who played for and coached alongside Moore.

The credo says it plainly: "I am because of Us."
